\"deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1\": {\"mmlu\": 0.890, \"helm\": 0.84},\n    \"google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it\": {\"mmlu\": 0.720, \"helm\": 0.70},\n}\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass CallResult:\n    success: bool\n    response_text: str\n    parsed: str | int | None\n    input_tokens: int\n    output_tokens: int\n    cost_usd: float\n    latency_s: float\n    error: str | None = None\n    raw: dict | None = None\n\n\n# ---- response normalization ------------------------------------------------\n#\n# v2 domains:\n#   logic        : V / I  (valid / invalid syllogism)\n#   arithmetic   : integer answer, or YES/NO on negation\n#   reading      : YES/NO (boolean), entity/day, or 2-way MCQ \"A\"/\"B\"\n#   fol          : TRUE / FALSE / UNCERTAIN\nLOGIC_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(V|I|v|i)\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\nINT_RE = re.compile(r\"-?\\d+\")\nYESNO_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(YES|NO|Y|N|TRUE|FALSE|T|F)\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\nFOL_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*(TRUE|FALSE|UNCERTAIN|T|F|U)\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\nMCQ_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\s*([AB])\\b\", re.IGNORECASE)\n\n\ndef normalize_response(text: str, domain: str, variant_role: str) -> str | int | None:\n    \"\"\"Pull the first canonical token from a (possibly chatty) LLM reply.\n\n    Domains:\n      logic      : V or I (syllogism validity)\n      arithmetic : int (seed/paraphrase/inverse), YES/NO (negation)\n      reading    : YES/NO (boolean), A/B (MCQ), or surface entity/day string\n      fol        : TRUE / FALSE / UNCERTAIN\n    \"\"\"\n    if text is None:\n        return None\n    txt = text.strip()\n    if not txt:\n        return None\n\n    # ----- Logic -----\n    if variant_role == \"negation\" and domain == \"logic\":\n        m = LOGIC_RE.match(txt)\n        if m:\n            return m.group(1).upper()\n        return None\n    if domain == \"logic\":\n        m = LOGIC_RE.match(txt)\n        if m:\n            return m.group(1).upper()\n        return None\n\n    # ----- FOL -----\n    if domain == \"fol\":\n        if variant_role == \"negation\":\n            # negation flips TRUE/FALSE; UNCERTAIN stays UNCERTAIN\n            m = FOL_RE.match(txt)\n            if m:\n                tok = m.group(1).upper()\n                return {\"T\": \"TRUE\", \"TRUE\": \"TRUE\",\n                        \"F\": \"FALSE\", \"FALSE\": \"FALSE\",\n                        \"U\": \"UNCERTAIN\", \"UNCERTAIN\": \"UNCERTAIN\"}.get(tok)\n            m = YESNO_RE.match(txt)\n            if m:\n                tok = m.group(1).upper()\n                return \"TRUE\" if tok in {\"YES\", \"Y\", \"TRUE\", \"T\"} else \"FALSE\"\n            return None\n        m = FOL_RE.match(txt)\n        if m:\n            tok = m.group(1).upper()\n            return {\"T\": \"TRUE\", \"TRUE\": \"TRUE\",\n # ----- Reading (multi-hop RC) -----\n    if domain == \"reading\":\n        if variant_role == \"negation\":\n            m = YESNO_RE.match(txt)\n            if m:\n                tok = m.group(1).upper()\n                return \"YES\" if tok in {\"YES\", \"Y\", \"TRUE\", \"T\"} else \"NO\"\n            return None\n        # MCQ -> A or B\n        m = MCQ_RE.match(txt)\n        if m:\n            return m.group(1).upper()\n        # YES/NO boolean questions\n        m = YESNO_RE.match(txt)\n        if m:\n            tok = m.group(1).upper()\n            return \"YES\" if tok in {\"YES\", \"Y\", \"TRUE\", \"T\"} else \"NO\"\n        # Otherwise: return the first token (entity/day). Caller (scoring_grm)\n        # uses the parsed result for a textual comparison against the oracle.\n        first = txt.split()[0].rstrip(\".,;:?!\") if txt else \"\"\n        return first if first else None\n\n    # ----- Arithmetic -----\n    if variant_role == \"negation\":\n        m = YESNO_RE.match(txt)\n        if m:\n            tok = m.group(1).upper()\n            return \"YES\" if tok in {\"YES\", \"Y\", \"TRUE\", \"T\"} else \"NO\"\n        return None\n    cleaned = txt.lstrip(\"$\u00a3\u20ac\u00a5\").strip()\n    m = INT_RE.match(cleaned)\n    if m:\n        try:\n            return int(m.group(0))\n        except ValueError:\n            return None\n    m = INT_RE.search(txt)\n    if m:\n        try:\n            return int(m.group(0))\n        except ValueError:\n            return None\n    return None\n\n\n# ---- cost catalog ---------------------------------------------------------\n\n_PRICING: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}\n_SUPPORTED: dict[str, set[str]] = {}\n\n\nasync def _load_catalog(session: aiohttp.ClientSession) -> None:\n    global _PRICING\n    if _PRICING:\n        return\n    try:\n        async with session.get(\n            \"https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models\",\n            timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=30),\n        ) as resp:\n            data = await resp.json(content_type=None)\n            for entry in data.get(\"data\", []):\n                name = entry.get(\"id\")\n                if not name:\n                    continue\n                p = entry.get(\"pricing\") or {}\n                try:\n                    _PRICING[name] = (\n                        float(p.get(\"prompt\", 0) or 0),\n                        float(p.get(\"completion\", 0) or 0),\n                    )\n                except (TypeError, ValueError):\n                    continue\n                sp = entry.get(\"supported_parameters\") or []\n                _SUPPORTED[name.lower()] = set(sp)\n    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001\n        logger.warning(f\"Catalog fetch failed: {exc}; falling back to local prices\")\n\n\ndef compute_cost_usd(model: str, in_tok: int, out_tok: int) -> float:\n    \"\"\"USD cost for a call, using the catalog (or local fallback).\"\"\"\n    price = _PRICING.get(model)\n    if price:\n        return round(in_tok * price[0] + out_tok * price[1], 8)\n    info = DEFAULT_MODEL_PANEL.get(model)\n    if info is None:\n        return 0.0\n    return round(in_tok * info[\"in_price\"] + out_tok * info[\"out_price\"], 8)\n\n\n# ---- async caller ---------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass CostLedger:\n    \"\"\"Tracks cumulative spend; raises SpendExceeded past the cap.\"\"\"\n    budget_usd: float\n    warn_usd: float = 2.00\n    critical_usd: float = 2.50\n    total_spent: float = 0.0\n    spend_log: list[dict] = field(default_factory=list)\n    lock: asyncio.Lock | None = None  # set after construction\n\n    def __post_init__(self):\n        if self.lock is None:\n            # asyncio.Lock requires a running loop; defer creation.\n            self.lock = None\n\n    async def _get_lock(self) -> asyncio.Lock:\n        if self.lock is None:\n            self.lock = asyncio.Lock()\n        return self.lock\n\n    async def add(self, cost: float, **meta) -> bool:\n        lock = await self._get_lock()\n        async with lock:\n            self.total_spent += cost\n            self.spend_log.append({\"ts\": time.time(), \"cost\": cost, **meta})\n            if self.total_spent >= self.budget_usd:\n                raise SpendExceeded(\n                    f\"OpenRouter spend ${self.total_spent:.4f} >= budget ${self.budget_usd:.2f}\"\n                )\n            if self.total_spent >= self.critical_usd:\n                logger.critical(f\"OpenRouter spend ${self.total_spent:.4f} >= ${self.critical_usd:.2f}\")\n            elif self.total_spent >= self.warn_usd:\n                logger.warning(f\"OpenRouter spend ${self.total_spent:.4f} >= ${self.warn_usd:.2f}\")\n            return True\n\n\nclass SpendExceeded(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"Raised when the cumulative OpenRouter bill exceeds the cap.\"\"\"\n\n\nasync def call_one(\n    session: aiohttp.ClientSession,\n    *,\n    model: str,\n    system: str,\n    user: str,\n    max_tokens: int = 16,\n    temperature: float = 0.0,\n    domain: str,\n    variant_role: str,\n    timeout_s: float = 60.0,\n) -> CallResult:\n    \"\"\"Make a single OpenRouter call with retries and parse the response.\"\"\"\n    headers = {\n        \"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {os.environ.get('OPENROUTER_API_KEY', '')}\",\n        \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\",\n    }\n    # Use chat/completions; for free-tier models that mandate reasoning we set\n    # reasoning.effort=\"low\" to keep them from spending the entire max_tokens\n    # budget on reasoning tokens. Paid models don't need this and would reject\n    # unknown params, so we only set it for :free models.\n    payload = {\n        \"model\": model,\n        \"max_tokens\": max_tokens,\n        \"temperature\": temperature,\n        \"messages\": [\n            {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": system},\n            {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": user},\n        ],\n    }\n    if model.endswith(\":free\") or \":free-\" in model:\n        payload[\"reasoning\"] = {\"effort\": \"low\"}\n    started = time.monotonic()\n    last_err: str | None = None\n\n    async def _attempt() -> CallResult:\n        nonlocal last_err\n        async with session.post(\n            API_URL,\n            json=payload,\n            headers=headers,\n            timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=timeout_s),\n        ) as resp:\n            txt = await resp.text()\n            if resp.status != 200:\n                raise OpenRouterHTTPError(resp.status, txt[:300])\n            try:\n                data = json.loads(txt)\n            except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:\n                raise OpenRouterHTTPError(resp.status, f\"json: {exc}\") from exc\n        # ---- extract output (chat/completions format) --------------------\n        output_text = \"\"\n        try:\n            choices = data.get(\"choices\") or []\n            if choices:\n                msg = choices[0].get(\"message\") or {}\n                output_text = msg.get(\"content\") or \"\"\n        except Exception:\n            output_text = \"\"\n        # Fallbacks for non-standard layouts\n        if not output_text:\n            output_text = data.get(\"output_text\", \"\") or \"\"\n        if not output_text:\n            for item in data.get(\"output\", []) or []:\n                if item.get(\"type\") == \"message\":\n                    content = item.get(\"content\") or []\n                    if content and isinstance(content[0], dict):\n                        output_text = content[0].get(\"text\", \"\")\n                    elif isinstance(content, str):\n                        output_text = content\n        usage = data.get(\"usage\", {}) or {}\n        in_tok = int(usage.get(\"prompt_tokens\", 0) or usage.get(\"input_tokens\", 0) or 0)\n        out_tok = int(usage.get(\"completion_tokens\", 0) or usage.get(\"output_tokens\", 0) or 0)\n        cost = compute_cost_usd(model, in_tok, out_tok)\n        parsed = normalize_response(output_text, domain, variant_role)\n        return CallResult(\n            success=True,\n            response_text=output_text,\n            parsed=parsed,\n            input_tokens=in_tok,\n            output_tokens=out_tok,\n            cost_usd=cost,\n            latency_s=time.monotonic() - started,\n            raw=data,\n        )\n\n    try:\n        async for attempt in AsyncRetrying(\n            stop=stop_after_attempt(4),\n            wait=wait_exponential(multiplier=2.0, min=2.0, max=30.0),\n            retry=retry_if_exception_type((OpenRouterHTTPError, aiohttp.ClientError, asyncio.TimeoutError)),\n            reraise=True,\n        ):\n            with attempt:\n                try:\n                    return await _attempt()\n                except OpenRouterHTTPError as exc:\n                    last_err = f\"HTTP {exc.status}: {exc.body[:120]}\"\n                    if exc.status in (400, 401, 403, 404):\n                        # unrecoverable; do not retry\n                        raise\n                    if exc.status == 429:\n                        # rate limited; sleep longer than the backoff schedule\n                        wait = float(os.environ.get(\"OR_429_WAIT_S\", \"30\"))\n                        logger.warning(f\"429 from {payload['model']}: sleeping {wait:.0f}s before retry\")\n                        await asyncio.sleep(wait)\n                    raise\n    except (OpenRouterHTTPError, aiohttp.ClientError, asyncio.TimeoutError) as exc:\n        return CallResult(\n            success=False,\n            response_text=\"\",\n            parsed=None,\n            input_tokens=0,\n            output_tokens=0,\n            cost_usd=0.0,\n            latency_s=time.monotonic() - started,\n            error=str(exc)[:200] or last_err or \"unknown error\",\n        )\n    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001\n        return CallResult(\n            success=False,\n            response_text=\"\",\n            parsed=None,\n            input_tokens=0,\n            output_tokens=0,\n            cost_usd=0.0,\n            latency_s=time.monotonic() - started,\n            error=str(exc)[:200],\n        )\n\n\nclass OpenRouterHTTPError(Exception):\n    def __init__(self, status: int, body: str):\n        super().__init__(f\"HTTP {status}: {body}\")\n        self.status = status\n        self.body = body\n\n\n# ---- batch driver ---------------------------------------------------------\n\nasync def query_panel(\n    panel: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],\n    clusters: list[dict],\n    *,\n    ledger: CostLedger,\n    concurrency: int = 40,\n    log_path: Path | None = None,\n    dry_run: bool = False,\n    requests_per_minute: float = 12.0,\n) -> dict[str, list[CallResult]]:\n    \"\"\"Query every (model, cluster, variant) cell concurrently.\n\n    Returns a nested dict {model_name: [CallResult per (cluster_idx, variant)]}.\n    Each model's list has length len(clusters) * 4, indexed by ci * 4 + j\n    where j is in [0..3] for roles ['seed','paraphrase','negation','<4th>'].\n\n    A global token-bucket rate limiter enforces `requests_per_minute` calls\n    across the entire sweep so that we stay below OpenRouter's free-tier\n    per-minute quota even when the per-request concurrency is high.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Build the list of work items deterministically.\n    # Flat layout: model -> list index aligned with the cluster order.\n    work: list[tuple[str, int, int, str, str, str]] = []\n    for m in panel:\n        for ci, c in enumerate(clusters):\n            for j, (role, variant) in enumerate(c[\"variants\"].items()):\n                domain = c[\"domain\"]\n                sys_msg = _system_message(domain, role)\n                work.append((m, ci, j, role, variant[\"question\"], domain, sys_msg))\n\n    results: dict[str, list[CallResult | None]] = {\n        m: [None] * (len(clusters) * 4) for m in panel\n    }\n    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)\n\n    # Token-bucket rate limiter: at any moment we hold at most `bucket_capacity`\n    # tokens; one token is added every `interval` seconds. To avoid holding the\n    # lock across an `asyncio.sleep`, the consume helper returns a future that\n    # resolves only when a token is available \u2014 and a single background task\n    # refills the bucket.\n    rpm = max(1.0, float(requests_per_minute))\n    interval = 60.0 / rpm\n    bucket_capacity = max(1.0, rpm)\n    bucket_state = {\n        \"tokens\": bucket_capacity,\n        \"last\": time.monotonic(),\n        \"waiters\": [],  # list of asyncio.Event per waiter\n    }\n    bucket_lock = asyncio.Lock()\n\n    async def _refill():\n        while True:\n            await asyncio.sleep(interval)\n            async with bucket_lock:\n                now = time.monotonic()\n                elapsed = now - bucket_state[\"last\"]\n                refill = elapsed / interval\n                if refill >= 1.0:\n                    add = int(refill)\n                    bucket_state[\"tokens\"] = min(bucket_capacity, bucket_state[\"tokens\"] + add)\n                    bucket_state[\"last\"] += add * interval\n                # Wake up as many waiters as we have tokens for\n                while bucket_state[\"waiters\"] and bucket_state[\"tokens\"] >= 1.0:\n                    bucket_state[\"tokens\"] -= 1.0\n                    ev = bucket_state[\"waiters\"].pop(0)\n                    ev.set()\n\n    async def _consume():\n        async with bucket_lock:\n            if bucket_state[\"tokens\"] >= 1.0:\n                bucket_state[\"tokens\"] -= 1.0\n                return\n            ev = asyncio.Event()\n            bucket_state[\"waiters\"].append(ev)\n        # Block until the refill task wakes us\n        await ev.wait()\n\n    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:\n        # Skip the catalog fetch \u2014 we use local DEFAULT_MODEL_PANEL prices.\n        logger.info(\"Session opened; skipping catalog fetch (using local prices)\")\n\n        if log_path is not None:\n            log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            log_f = log_path.open(\"w\")\n        else:\n            log_f = None\n\n        async def _one(model: str, ci: int, j: int, role: str, q: str, domain: str, sys_msg: str, dry_rng=None):\n            if not dry_run and (model.endswith(\":free\") or \":free-\" in model):\n                await _consume()\n            async with sem:\n                if dry_run:\n                    # Produce a deterministic but non-degenerate response. For\n                    # the smoke test we want the GRM to see a spread of\n                    # coherence scores so it can be fitted. Each model gets a\n                    # different \"ability\" via the per-model correctness prob.\n                    rng = dry_rng or random.Random(hash((model, ci, j)) & 0xFFFFFFFF)\n                    correctness = {\n                        \"openai/gpt-4o-mini\": 0.85,\n                        \"openai/gpt-4.1-mini\": 0.86,\n                        \"anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5\": 0.78,\n                        \"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4\": 0.90,\n                        \"google/gemini-2.5-flash\": 0.86,\n                        \"meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct\": 0.55,\n                        \"meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct\": 0.88,\n                        \"meta-llama/llama-3.2-3b-instruct\": 0.45,\n                        \"qwen/qwen-2.5-7b-instruct\": 0.65,\n                        \"qwen/qwen-2.5-72b-instruct\": 0.87,\n                        \"mistralai/mistral-small-24b-instruct-2501\": 0.50,\n                        \"mistralai/mistral-large-2407\": 0.80,\n                        \"mistralai/ministral-8b-2512\": 0.50,\n                        \"deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1\": 0.89,\n                        \"google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it\": 0.52,\n                    }.get(model, 0.6)\n                    is_correct = rng.random() < correctness\n                    text, parsed = _dry_run_response(rng, domain, role, is_correct)\n                    res = CallResult(\n                        success=parsed is not None,\n                        response_text=text or \"PARSE_FAIL\",\n                        parsed=parsed,\n                        input_tokens=120,\n                        output_tokens=4,\n                        cost_usd=0.0001,\n                        latency_s=0.0,\n                    )\n                else:\n                    res = await call_one(\n                        session,\n                        model=model,\n                        system=sys_msg,\n                        user=q,\n                        domain=domain,\n                        variant_role=role,\n                        max_tokens=16,\n                    )\n                await ledger.add(res.cost_usd, model=model, ci=ci, role=role)\n                if log_f is not None:\n                    log_f.write(json.dumps({\n                        \"model\": model,\n                        \"ci\": ci,\n                        \"j\": j,\n                        \"role\": role,\n                        \"q\": q[:200],\n                        \"ok\": res.success,\n                        \"parsed\": res.parsed if res.parsed is not None else str(res.error),\n                        \"in_tok\": res.input_tokens,\n                        \"out_tok\": res.output_tokens,\n                        \"cost_usd\": res.cost_usd,\n                        \"latency_s\": res.latency_s,\n                    }) + \"\\n\")\n                results[model][ci * 4 + j] = res\n\n        tasks = [_one(*w) for w in work]\n        refill_task = asyncio.create_task(_refill())\n        try:\n            await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=False)\n        finally:\n            refill_task.cancel()\n\n        if log_f is not None:\n            log_f.close()\n    # Cast None -> failure marker (shouldn't happen, but be defensive)\n    final: dict[str, list[CallResult]] = {}\n    for m, recs in results.items():\n        final[m] = [\n            r if r is not None else CallResult(\n                success=False, response_text=\"\", parsed=None,\n                input_tokens=0, output_tokens=0, cost_usd=0.0,\n                latency_s=0.0, error=\"missing_response\",\n            )\n            for r in recs\n        ]\n    return final\n\n\ndef _dry_run_response(rng: random.Random, domain: str, role: str, is_correct: bool):\n    \"\"\"Generate a synthetic dry-run response covering all four v2 domains.\n\n    Returns (text, parsed) where parsed is None for unparseable responses.\n    The `is_correct` flag biases whether the response matches the oracle for\n    the variant role; negation roles deliberately flip the response when the\n    model \"agrees\" with the negation.\n    \"\"\"\n    def _ok(text: str) -> bool:\n        return rng.random() < 0.95\n\n    if domain == \"logic\":\n        text = (\"V\" if rng.random() < 0.5 else \"I\") if _ok(\"\") else \"\"\n        parsed = \"V\" if text.startswith(\"V\") else (\"I\" if text.startswith(\"I\") else None)\n        if role == \"negation\" and is_correct and parsed is not None:\n            parsed = \"I\" if parsed == \"V\" else \"V\"\n        return text, parsed\n\n    if domain == \"fol\":\n        if rng.random() < 0.7:\n            choices = [\"TRUE\", \"FALSE\", \"UNCERTAIN\"]\n            text = choices[rng.randint(0, 2)]\n            parsed = text\n        else:\n            text = \"TRUE\" if rng.random() < 0.5 else \"FALSE\"\n            parsed = text\n        if role == \"negation\" and is_correct and parsed in {\"TRUE\", \"FALSE\"}:\n            parsed = \"FALSE\" if parsed == \"TRUE\" else \"TRUE\"\n        return text, parsed\n\n    if domain == \"reading\":\n        if role == \"negation\":\n            text = \"YES\" if rng.random() < 0.5 else \"NO\"\n            parsed = text\n            if is_correct:\n                # seed answer would be e.g. YES, negation answer is NO\n                parsed = \"NO\" if parsed == \"YES\" else \"YES\"\n            return text, parsed\n        # MCQ (A or B) for ~50% of dry runs; otherwise entity/string\n        if rng.random() < 0.5:\n            text = \"A\" if rng.random() < 0.5 else \"B\"\n            parsed = text\n            return text, parsed\n        # entity\n        text = \"Alice\" if rng.random() < 0.5 else \"Bob\"\n        parsed = text\n        return text, parsed\n\n    # arithmetic (default)\n    if role == \"negation\":\n        text = \"YES\" if rng.random() < 0.5 else \"NO\"\n        parsed = text\n        return text, parsed\n    n = rng.randint(2, 25)\n    text = str(n) if _ok(\"\") else \"\"\n    try:\n        parsed = int(text)\n    except ValueError:\n        parsed = None\n    return text, parsed\n\n\ndef _system_message(domain: str, role: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Per-variant system message \u2014 keeps the model's response space narrow.\"\"\"\n    if domain == \"logic\":\n        return (\n            \"You must answer with exactly one character: V if the argument is valid, \"\n            \"I if it is invalid. For negation questions, still answer V or I based on \"\n            \"the truth of the original (negated) claim. No explanation, no other text.\"\n        )\n    if domain == \"fol\":\n        return (\n            \"You must answer with exactly one word: TRUE, FALSE, or UNCERTAIN. \"\n            \"TRUE if the conclusion logically follows from the premises, \"\n            \"FALSE if it contradicts them, UNCERTAIN if the premises are insufficient. \"\n            \"For negation questions, give the opposite truth value (TRUE<->FALSE, \"\n            \"but UNCERTAIN stays UNCERTAIN). No explanation, no other text.\"\n        )\n    if domain == \"reading\":\n        if role == \"negation\":\n            return (\n                \"You must answer with exactly one word: YES or NO. \"\n                \"No explanation, no other text.\"\n            )\n        return (\n            \"You must answer with ONLY a single token: the named entity (person, \"\n            \"place, day) or YES/NO for a boolean question, or A/B for a multiple \"\n            \"choice question. No explanation, no other text.\"\n        )\n    # arithmetic\n    if role == \"negation\":\n        return (\n            \"You must answer with exactly one word: YES or NO. \"\n            \"No explanation, no other text.\"\n        )\n    return (\n        \"You must answer with only the integer result. No explanation, \"\n        \"no other text.\"\n    )\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Natural contamination (system-prompt injection)\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nasync def _call_one_with_system(\n    session: aiohttp.ClientSession,\n    *,\n    model: str,\n    system: str,\n    user: str,\n    domain: str,\n    variant_role: str,\n    max_tokens: int = 16,\n    temperature: float = 0.0,\n    timeout_s: float = 60.0,\n) -> CallResult:\n    \"\"\"One-shot variant of call_one that allows a caller-provided system prompt.\n\n    Used by natural contamination so we can prepend an oracle hint to the\n    system prompt. Reuses the same retry / cost logic as call_one().\n    \"\"\"\n    headers = {\n        \"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {os.environ.get('OPENROUTER_API_KEY', '')}\",\n        \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\",\n    }\n    payload = {\n        \"model\": model,\n        \"max_tokens\": max_tokens,\n        \"temperature\": temperature,\n        \"messages\": [\n            {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": system},\n            {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": user},\n        ],\n    }\n    if model.endswith(\":free\") or \":free-\" in model:\n        payload[\"reasoning\"] = {\"effort\": \"low\"}\n    started = time.monotonic()\n    try:\n        async with session.post(\n            API_URL,\n            json=payload,\n            headers=headers,\n            timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=timeout_s),\n        ) as resp:\n            txt = await resp.text()\n            if resp.status != 200:\n                return CallResult(False, \"\", None, 0, 0, 0.0, time.monotonic()-started,\n                                  error=f\"HTTP {resp.status}: {txt[:200]}\")\n            data = json.loads(txt)\n        out_text = \"\"\n        choices = data.get(\"choices\") or []\n        if choices:\n            msg = choices[0].get(\"message\") or {}\n            out_text = msg.get(\"content\") or \"\"\n        usage = data.get(\"usage\", {}) or {}\n        in_tok = int(usage.get(\"prompt_tokens\", 0) or usage.get(\"input_tokens\", 0) or 0)\n        out_tok = int(usage.get(\"completion_tokens\", 0) or usage.get(\"output_tokens\", 0) or 0)\n        cost = compute_cost_usd(model, in_tok, out_tok)\n        parsed = normalize_response(out_text, domain, variant_role)\n        return CallResult(True, out_text, parsed, in_tok, out_tok, cost,\n                          time.monotonic()-started, raw=data)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        return CallResult(False, \"\", None, 0, 0, 0.0, time.monotonic()-started,\n                          error=str(exc)[:200])\n\n\nasync def query_contaminated(\n    panel: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],\n    clusters: list[dict],\n    *,\n    target_model: str,\n    contaminated_ids: set[str],\n    oracle_by_id: dict[str, str],\n    ledger: CostLedger,\n    concurrency: int = 10,\n    requests_per_minute: float = 12.0,\n) -> list[CallResult]:\n    \"\"\"Re-query the target model on contaminated clusters with a system prompt\n    that injects the seed oracle.\n\n    For non-contaminated clusters, returns a sentinel CallResult with\n    parsed=None and cost=0 (the scoring layer will reuse the clean response).\n    \"\"\"\n    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(concurrency)\n    rpm = max(1.0, float(requests_per_minute))\n    interval = 60.0 / rpm\n    bucket_state = {\"tokens\": rpm, \"last\": time.monotonic(), \"waiters\": []}\n    bucket_lock = asyncio.Lock()\n\n    async def _refill():\n        while True:\n            await asyncio.sleep(interval)\n            async with bucket_lock:\n                now = time.monotonic()\n                elapsed = now - bucket_state[\"last\"]\n                refill = elapsed / interval\n                if refill >= 1.0:\n                    add = int(refill)\n                    bucket_state[\"tokens\"] = min(rpm, bucket_state[\"tokens\"] + add)\n                    bucket_state[\"last\"] += add * interval\n                while bucket_state[\"waiters\"] and bucket_state[\"tokens\"] >= 1.0:\n                    bucket_state[\"tokens\"] -= 1.0\n                    ev = bucket_state[\"waiters\"].pop(0)\n                    ev.set()\n\n    async def _consume():\n        async with bucket_lock:\n            if bucket_state[\"tokens\"] >= 1.0:\n                bucket_state[\"tokens\"] -= 1.0\n                return\n            ev = asyncio.Event()\n            bucket_state[\"waiters\"].append(ev)\n        await ev.wait()\n\n    # Build the work list: only contaminated clusters, all 4 variants\n    work = []\n    for ci, c in enumerate(clusters):\n        if c[\"cluster_id\"] not in contaminated_ids:\n            continue\n        for role, variant in c[\"variants\"].items():\n            work.append((ci, role, variant[\"question\"], c[\"domain\"]))\n\n    results: list[CallResult | None] = [None] * len(work)\n\n    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:\n        async def _one(i: int, ci: int, role: str, q: str, domain: str):\n            if not target_model.endswith(\":free\") and \":free-\" not in target_model:\n                pass  # only throttle free tier models\n            else:\n                await _consume()\n            async with sem:\n                base_sys = _system_message(domain, role)\n                oracle = oracle_by_id.get(ci, \"\")\n                contaminated_sys = (\n                    base_sys\n                    + \"\\n\\n--- CONTEXT (you may have seen this question before) ---\\n\"\n                    + f\"The correct answer is {oracle}.\\n\"\n How many {item} does {name1} have in total?\",\n        \"answer\": a * b,\n    }\n\n\nARITHMETIC_TEMPLATES = [\n    (\"AS1\", _as1),\n    (\"AS2\", _as2),\n    (\"AS3\", _as3),\n    (\"AS4\", _as4),\n    (\"AS5\", _as5),\n    (\"AS6\", _as6),\n    (\"AS7\", _as7),\n    (\"AS8\", _as8),\n    (\"AS9\", _as9),\n    (\"AS10\", _as10),\n    (\"AS11\", _as11),\n    (\"AS12\", _as12),\n]\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Variant construction helpers\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _contrapositive(premises: str, conclusion: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Crude but consistent contrapositive rephrasing.\n\n    The original conclusion says \"all A are C\" / \"no A are C\" / \"some A are C\"\n    / \"some A are not C\". We rephrase as a meta-question asking whether the\n    contrapositive holds: \"If something is not C, can it still be A?\" \u2014 to\n    which the answer is the OPPOSITE of the original. So actually we set the\n    *expected oracle answer* for the contrapositive variant equal to the\n    original label (it is logically equivalent).\n    \"\"\"\n    # Pull the conclusion phrase (after the period), strip the \"Therefore,\" prefix\n    tail = conclusion.strip()\n    if tail.lower().startswith(\"therefore,\"):\n        tail = tail[len(\"therefore,\"):].strip()\n    # Build: \"Is the following also true: <tail>?\" \u2014 answer remains label.\n    tail_clean = tail.rstrip(\"?. \")\n    return f\"Is the following claim also true: {tail_clean}?\"\n\n\ndef _paraphrase_logic(premises: str, conclusion: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Noun-swap paraphrase: replace any A/B/C placeholders from the seed pool\n    with fresh ones from the paraphrase pool. Strip the leading \"All X are Y.\"\n    and rephrase with the canonical template form. Because we only swap the\n    *content* of the noun slots, the syllogism's logical form \u2014 and therefore\n    its truth value \u2014 is preserved.\n    \"\"\"\n    # We rely on the seed having been built from {A}, {B}, {C} slots already\n    # filled; the paraphrased cluster rebuilds the same template with new\n    # nouns, so the actual paraphrase call here is identity (the variant is\n    # generated upstream in `_build_logic_cluster`).\n    return premises + \" \" + conclusion\n\n\ndef _negation_logic(conclusion: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Negation variant: the oracle answer flips.\n\n    Returns (question, opposite_label).\n    \"\"\"\n    tail = conclusion.strip()\n    if tail.lower().startswith(\"therefore,\"):\n        tail = tail[len(\"therefore,\"):].strip()\n    # Question is \"Is it NOT the case that <conclusion>?\" \u2014 yes iff conclusion is false.\n    # The model's answer to \"Is the conclusion invalid?\" flips the original label.\n    tail_clean = tail.rstrip(\"?. \")\n    question = f\"Is it NOT the case that {tail_clean}?\"\n    return question, \"FLIPPED\"  # marker; the scoring layer flips the response\n\n\ndef _inverse_arithmetic(seed_question: str, seed_answer: int, a: int) -> tuple[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Inverse variant for arithmetic: 'additive identity' \u2014 ask for the first\n    addend (a). The oracle answer differs from the seed, so this is the\n    'inverse/control' role rather than 'contrapositive equivalent'.\n    \"\"\"\n    return (\n        f\"(Inverse) Consider a problem with the same setup as: '{seed_question}'. \"\n        f\"What was the original starting quantity (the first number mentioned)?\",\n        a,\n    )\n\n\ndef _negation_arithmetic(seed_question: str, seed_answer: int) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Negation variant for arithmetic: a yes/no question with a *fixed*\n    deterministic oracle (independent of the model's seed answer).\n\n    We ask \"Is the answer to this problem equal to <wrong_value>?\" \u2014 the\n    oracle is \"NO\" (since the wrong value is, by construction, not the\n    seed answer). The coherence layer treats this as a binary claim the\n    model can answer YES/NO. We do NOT fold it into the same response\n    space as the seed; instead, the relational invariant is that the\n    negation's oracle is fixed and the model must agree with it.\n    \"\"\"\n    wrong = seed_answer + 1\n    question = (\n        f\"Consider: {seed_question} Is the answer to this problem equal to {wrong}? \"\n        f\"Answer YES or NO only.\"\n    )\n    return question, \"NO\"\n\n\ndef _paraphrase_arithmetic(seed_question: str, seed_answer: int, name1: str,\n                           name2: str, item: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Noun-swap paraphrase. The seed question will be rebuilt upstream with\n    fresh nouns; here we just return the seed form.\"\"\"\n    return seed_question\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Cluster builders\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass Variant:\n    role: str            # 'seed' | 'paraphrase' | 'negation' | 'contrapositive' | 'inverse'\n    question: str\n    oracle: str | int    # canonical answer; for negation it is 'FLIPPED'\n    raw_question: str = \"\"  # original phrasing for logging\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass MIC:\n    cluster_id: str\n    domain: str           # 'logic' | 'arithmetic'\n    template_id: str\n    variants: dict[str, Variant] = field(default_factory=dict)\n    answers: dict[str, str | int] = field(default_factory=dict)\n    relations: dict[str, bool] = field(default_factory=dict)\n    difficulty_hint: str = \"medium\"\n    oracle_correct: str | int = \"\"\n\n\ndef _build_logic_cluster(idx: int, rng: random.Random) -> MIC:\n    \"\"\"Build one logic MIC using a randomly-chosen template + nouns.\"\"\"\n    template_id, builder = rng.choice(LOGIC_TEMPLATES)\n    A = rng.choice(LOGIC_NOUNS)\n    B = rng.choice([n for n in LOGIC_NOUNS if n != A])\n    C = rng.choice([n for n in LOGIC_NOUNS if n not in (A, B)])\n    premises, conclusion, label = builder(A, B, C)\n    seed_question = premises + \" \" + conclusion\n\n    # Paraphrase: same template, fresh nouns from the paraphrase pool\n    A2 = rng.choice(LOGIC_NOUNS_PARAPHRASE)\n    B2 = rng.choice([n for n in LOGIC_NOUNS_PARAPHRASE if n != A2])\n    C2 = rng.choice([n for n in LOGIC_NOUNS_PARAPHRASE if n not in (A2, B2)])\n    _, _, _ = builder(A2, B2, C2)\n    p2_premises, p2_conclusion, _ = builder(A2, B2, C2)\n    paraphrase_question = p2_premises + \" \" + p2_conclusion\n\n    # Negation: question + flipped\n    neg_question, neg_label = _negation_logic(conclusion)\n\n    # Contrapositive: rephrasing that holds iff original does\n    contra_question = _contrapositive(premises, conclusion)\n\n    cluster_id = f\"logic_{idx:04d}\"\n\n    mic = MIC(\n        cluster_id=cluster_id,\n        domain=\"logic\",\n        template_id=template_id,\n        difficulty_hint=_difficulty_hint_logic(template_id),\n        oracle_correct=label,\n    )\n    mic.variants = {\n        \"seed\": Variant(role=\"seed\", question=seed_question, oracle=label, raw_question=seed_question),\n        \"paraphrase\": Variant(role=\"paraphrase\", question=paraphrase_question, oracle=label, raw_question=paraphrase_question),\n        \"negation\": Variant(role=\"negation\", question=neg_question, oracle=neg_label, raw_question=neg_question),\n        \"contrapositive\": Variant(role=\"contrapositive\", question=contra_question, oracle=label, raw_question=contra_question),\n    }\n    mic.answers = {\n        \"seed\": label,\n        \"paraphrase\": label,\n        \"negation\": \"FLIPPED\",\n        \"contrapositive\": label,\n    }\n    mic.relations = {\n        \"paraphrase_eq_seed\": True,\n        \"negation_eq_not_seed\": True,\n        \"contrapositive_eq_seed\": True,\n    }\n    return mic\n\n\ndef _difficulty_hint_logic(template_id: str) -> str:\n    if template_id in (\"T1\", \"T4\", \"T5\", \"T10\"):\n        return \"easy\"\n    if template_id in (\"T2\", \"T7\", \"T11\", \"T12\"):\n        return \"medium\"\n    return \"hard\"\n\n\ndef _build_arithmetic_cluster(idx: int, rng: random.Random) -> MIC:\n    \"\"\"Build one arithmetic MIC.\"\"\"\n    template_id, builder = rng.choice(ARITHMETIC_TEMPLATES)\n\n    # Generate template-appropriate operands (all in [2,25], integer results).\n    # Per-template constraints: AS2 needs a > b; AS7 needs a % b == 0;\n    # AS11 picks big/small internally; AS12 needs a*b <= 100 (no absurd counts).\n    for _ in range(80):\n        a = rng.randint(2, 25)\n        b = rng.randint(2, 25)\n        c = rng.randint(2, 25)\n        # Per-template constraints\n        if template_id == \"AS2\" and a <= b:\n            continue\n        if template_id == \"AS7\" and (a % b != 0):\n            continue\n        if template_id == \"AS12\" and a * b > 100:\n            continue\n        name1 = rng.choice(NAMES_A)\n        name2 = rng.choice([n for n in NAMES_B if n != name1])\n        item = rng.choice(ITEMS)\n        out = builder(name1, name2, item, a, b, c)\n        ans = out[\"answer\"]\n        # require positive integer result\n        if isinstance(ans, int) and ans > 0:\n            break\n    else:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"arithmetic generator failed to produce positive answer\")\n\n    seed_question = out[\"question\"]\n    seed_answer = out[\"answer\"]\n\n    # Paraphrase: rebuild with fresh names + items\n    name1b = rng.choice(NAMES_B)\n    name2b = rng.choice([n for n in NAMES_A if n != name1b])\n    itemb = rng.choice(ITEMS_PARAPHRASE)\n    out2 = builder(name1b, name2b, itemb, a, b, c)\n    paraphrase_question = out2[\"question\"]\n\n    # Negation: a yes/no question whose oracle is \"NO\" (the wrong value is\n    # by construction not the seed answer).\n    neg_question, neg_label = _negation_arithmetic(seed_question, seed_answer)\n\n    # Inverse: ask for the original first addend\n    inv_question, inv_answer = _inverse_arithmetic(seed_question, seed_answer, a)\n\n    cluster_id = f\"arith_{idx:04d}\"\n    mic = MIC(\n        cluster_id=cluster_id,\n        domain=\"arithmetic\",\n        template_id=template_id,\n        difficulty_hint=_difficulty_hint_arith(seed_answer),\n        oracle_correct=seed_answer,\n    )\n    mic.variants = {\n        \"seed\": Variant(role=\"seed\", question=seed_question, oracle=seed_answer, raw_question=seed_question),\n        \"paraphrase\": Variant(role=\"paraphrase\", question=paraphrase_question, oracle=seed_answer, raw_question=paraphrase_question),\n        \"negation\": Variant(role=\"negation\", question=neg_question, oracle=neg_label, raw_question=neg_question),\n        \"inverse\": Variant(role=\"inverse\", question=inv_question, oracle=inv_answer, raw_question=inv_question),\n    }\n    mic.answers = {\n        \"seed\": seed_answer,\n        \"paraphrase\": seed_answer,\n        \"negation\": \"NO\",\n        \"inverse\": inv_answer,\n    }\n    mic.relations = {\n        \"paraphrase_eq_seed\": True,\n        \"negation_eq_no\": True,\n        \"inverse_distinct\": True,  # inverse has a different oracle answer\n    }\n    return mic\n\n\ndef _difficulty_hint_arith(ans: int) -> str:\n    if ans <= 10:\n        return \"easy\"\n    if ans <= 25:\n        return \"medium\"\n    return \"hard\"\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Public entrypoint\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef generate_mics(n_logic: int, n_arithmetic: int, seed: int = 0) -> list[dict]:\n    \"\"\"Build the requested number of MICs across both domains.\"\"\"\n    rng = random.Random(seed)\n    clusters: list[MIC] = []\n    for i in range(n_logic):\n        clusters.append(_build_logic_cluster(i, rng))\n    for i in range(n_arithmetic):\n        clusters.append(_build_arithmetic_cluster(i, rng))\n    # Shuffle so logic and arithmetic are interleaved\n    rng.shuffle(clusters)\n    return [asdict(c) for c in clusters]\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Lightweight self-test\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sample = generate_mics(n_logic=3, n_arithmetic=3, seed=42)\n    import json\n    print(json.dumps(sample, indent=2, default=str))", "new_content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Stage 1: Metamorphic Item Cluster (MIC) generator.\n\nProduces deterministic clusters in two domains \u2014 propositional syllogisms and\narithmetic word problems. Each cluster carries four variants: seed, paraphrase,\nnegation, and (for logic) contrapositive / (for arithmetic) inverse \u2014 plus the\noracle (ground-truth) answer and a difficulty hint.\n\nPure Python / stdlib. No API spend, runs on CPU.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport random\nimport re\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, asdict, field\nfrom typing import Callable\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Noun / proper-name pools. Distinct noun sets are reserved per domain so\n# paraphrase clauses never share vocabulary with the seed.\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nLOGIC_NOUNS = [\n    \"doctors\", \"lawyers\", \"teachers\", \"engineers\", \"scientists\", \"writers\",\n    \"farmers\", \"musicians\", \"athletes\", \"drivers\", \"students\", \"workers\",\n    \"artists\", \"soldiers\", \"pilots\", \"chefs\", \"painters\", \"dancers\",\n    \"singers\", \"judges\", \"actors\", \"nurses\", \"carpenters\", \"miners\",\n    \"plumbers\", \"gardeners\", \"tailors\", \"designers\", \"explorers\", \"astronauts\",\n    \"metals\", \"gases\", \"liquids\", \"minerals\", \"vegetables\", \"fruits\",\n    \"flowers\", \"trees\", \"insects\", \"fish\", \"birds\", \"reptiles\",\n    \"tools\", \"vehicles\", \"buildings\", \"devices\", \"garments\", \"furniture\",\n    \"documents\", \"machines\", \"weapons\", \"instruments\", \"vessels\", \"structures\",\n]\n\nLOGIC_NOUNS_PARAPHRASE = [\n    \"philosophers\", \"veterinarians\", \"architects\", \"dentists\", \"librarians\",\n    \"journalists\", \"bakers\", \"cobblers\", \"locksmiths\", \"masons\", \"opticians\",\n    \"pharmacists\", \"surveyors\", \"barbers\", \"butchers\", \"fishermen\", \"hunters\",\n    \"spices\", \"cereals\", \"mushrooms\", \"berries\", \"shells\", \"stones\",\n    \"crystals\", \"fossils\", \"poems\", \"novels\", \"songs\", \"stories\",\n    \"diamonds\", \"pearls\", \"coins\", \"stamps\", \"puzzles\", \"toys\",\n    \"candles\", \"mirrors\", \"lanterns\", \"rugs\", \"blankets\", \"curtains\",\n]\n\nNAMES_A = [\n    \"Alice\", \"Brian\", \"Carmen\", \"Diego\", \"Esme\", \"Felix\", \"Greta\", \"Hassan\",\n    \"Inez\", \"Jules\", \"Keiko\", \"Liam\", \"Maya\", \"Noah\", \"Olive\", \"Pedro\",\n    \"Quinn\", \"Rosa\", \"Sami\", \"Tomas\", \"Uma\", \"Vince\", \"Wren\", \"Xenia\",\n    \"Yara\", \"Zane\",\n]\nNAMES_B = [\n    \"Beatrice\", \"Caleb\", \"Daria\", \"Eitan\", \"Farah\", \"Gideon\", \"Hana\",\n    \"Ivan\", \"Jada\", \"Karim\", \"Lila\", \"Marco\", \"Nadia\", \"Owen\", \"Priya\",\n    \"Quincy\", \"Rafael\", \"Selma\", \"Tariq\", \"Ula\", \"Vera\", \"Wesley\", \"Ximena\",\n    \"Yusuf\", \"Zara\",\n]\n\nITEMS = [\n    \"apples\", \"books\", \"pencils\", \"marbles\", \"cookies\", \"stamps\", \"stickers\",\n    \"cards\", \"shells\", \"toys\", \"buttons\", \"ribbons\", \"beads\", \"pebbles\",\n    \"candies\", \"oranges\", \"lemons\", \"plums\", \"acorns\", \"feathers\", \"pearls\",\n    \"coins\", \"rubber bands\", \"paper clips\",\n]\n\nITEMS_PARAPHRASE = [\n    \"trading cards\", \"figurines\", \"postcards\", \"souvenir spoons\", \"fossils\",\n    \"gemstones\", \"marbles of glass\", \"scraps of paper\", \"buttons of brass\",\n    \"ribbons of silk\", \"beads of jade\", \"pebbles of quartz\", \"feathers of blue\",\n    \"pearls of pink\", \"stones of jade\", \"smooth chestnuts\",\n    \"silver coins\", \"tiny bells\", \"tiny skulls\", \"wax seals\", \"lacquered fans\",\n    \"candy wrappers\", \"tin whistles\", \"tiny lamps\",\n]\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Logic (syllogism) templates\n#\n# Each template returns (premise_a, premise_b, conclusion, label) where\n# label is the oracle answer \u2014 'V' for valid, 'I' for invalid.\n# The slots {A}, {B}, {C} are filled with concrete nouns.\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nLOGIC_TEMPLATES: list[tuple[str, Callable[[str, str, str], tuple[str, str, str, str]]]] = [\n    (\n        \"T1\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"All {A} are {B}. All {B} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, all {A} are {C}.\",\n            \"V\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T2\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"All {A} are {B}. Some {B} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, all {A} are {C}.\",\n            \"I\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T3\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"No {A} are {B}. All {B} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, no {A} are {C}.\",\n            \"I\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T4\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"All {A} are {B}. No {B} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, no {A} are {C}.\",\n            \"V\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T5\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"Some {A} are {B}. All {B} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, some {A} are {C}.\",\n            \"V\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T6\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"Some {A} are {B}. Some {B} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, some {A} are {C}.\",\n            \"I\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T7\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"All {A} are {B}. All {C} are {B}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, some {A} are {C}.\",\n            \"I\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T8\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"All {A} are {B}. All {B} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, some {A} are not {C}.\",\n            \"I\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T9\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"All {A} are {B}. All {A} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, some {B} are {C}.\",\n            \"I\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T10\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"All {A} are {B}. No {A} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, no {B} are {C}.\",\n            \"V\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T11\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"Some {A} are not {B}. All {B} are {C}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, some {A} are not {C}.\",\n            \"V\",\n        )\n    ),\n    (\n        \"T12\", lambda A, B, C: (\n            f\"All {A} are {B}. All {C} are not {B}.\",\n            f\"Therefore, no {A} are {C}.\",\n            \"V\",\n        )\n    ),\n]\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Arithmetic word-problem templates\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _int_str(a: int, b: int, c: int, name1: str, name2: str, item: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Empty marker; arithmetic templates compute via simple expressions.\"\"\"\n    return {\"_\": \"placeholder\"}\n\n\nARITHMETIC_TEMPLATES: list[tuple[str, Callable]] = []\n\n\ndef _as1(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name2} gives {name1} {b} more. How many {item} does {name1} have?\",\n        \"answer\": a + b,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as2(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name1} gives {name2} {b}. How many {item} does {name1} have left?\",\n        \"answer\": a - b,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as3(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name2} has {b} {item}. How many {item} do they have together?\",\n        \"answer\": a + b,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as4(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"A box has {a} {item}. {b} are taken out and {c} put in. How many {item} are in the box?\",\n        \"answer\": a - b + c,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as5(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{name1} is {a} years old. {name2} is {b} years older than {name1}. How old is {name2}?\",\n        \"answer\": a + b,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as6(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{name1} buys {a} {item} at $1 each. {name1} pays with a ${b} bill. How much change does {name1} receive?\",\n        \"answer\": b - a,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as7(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    # Ensure exact division for clean integer answers\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{a} {item} are split equally among {b} people. How many {item} does each person get?\",\n        \"answer\": a // b,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as8(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{name1} walks {a} km on day 1 and {b} km on day 2. What is the average distance walked per day?\",\n        \"answer\": (a + b) // 2,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as9(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    # Multi-step: 2x + y, with two operands.\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name1} finds {b} more, then loses half of what they now have. How many {item} does {name1} have?\",\n        \"answer\": (a + b) // 2,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as10(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    # Three-operand subtraction chain\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{name1} has {a} {item}. {name1} gives {b} to {name2} and then gives {c} to a third person. How many {item} does {name1} have left?\",\n        \"answer\": a - b - c,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as11(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    # Difference (subtraction) \u2014 requires identifying larger first\n    big = max(a, b)\n    small = min(a, b)\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"{name1} has {big} {item}. {name2} has {small}. How many more {item} does {name1} have than {name2}?\",\n        \"answer\": big - small,\n    }\n\n\ndef _as12(name1, name2, item, a, b, c):\n    # Multiplication (single-step)\n    return {\n        \"question\": f\"Each bag holds {a} {item}. {name1} buys {b} bags. How many {item} does {name1} have in total?\",\n        \"answer\": a * b,\n    }\n\n\nARITHMETIC_TEMPLATES = [\n    (\"AS1\", _as1),\n    (\"AS2\", _as2),\n    (\"AS3\", _as3),\n    (\"AS4\", _as4),\n    (\"AS5\", _as5),\n    (\"AS6\", _as6),\n    (\"AS7\", _as7),\n    (\"AS8\", _as8),\n    (\"AS9\", _as9),\n    (\"AS10\", _as10),\n    (\"AS11\", _as11),\n    (\"AS12\", _as12),\n]\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Variant construction helpers\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef _contrapositive(premises: str, conclusion: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Crude but consistent contrapositive rephrasing.\n\n    The original conclusion says \"all A are C\" / \"no A are C\" / \"some A are C\"\n    / \"some A are not C\". We rephrase as a meta-question asking whether the\n    contrapositive holds: \"If something is not C, can it still be A?\" \u2014 to\n    which the answer is the OPPOSITE of the original. So actually we set the\n    *expected oracle answer* for the contrapositive variant equal to the\n    original label (it is logically equivalent).\n    \"\"\"\n    # Pull the conclusion phrase (after the period), strip the \"Therefore,\" prefix\n    tail = conclusion.strip()\n    if tail.lower().startswith(\"therefore,\"):\n        tail = tail[len(\"therefore,\"):].strip()\n    # Build: \"Is the following also true: <tail>?\" \u2014 answer remains label.\n    tail_clean = tail.rstrip(\"?. \")\n    return f\"Is the following claim also true: {tail_clean}?\"\n\n\ndef _paraphrase_logic(premises: str, conclusion: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Noun-swap paraphrase: replace any A/B/C placeholders from the seed pool\n    with fresh ones from the paraphrase pool. Strip the leading \"All X are Y.\"\n    and rephrase with the canonical template form. Because we only swap the\n    *content* of the noun slots, the syllogism's logical form \u2014 and therefore\n    its truth value \u2014 is preserved.\n    \"\"\"\n    # We rely on the seed having been built from {A}, {B}, {C} slots already\n    # filled; the paraphrased cluster rebuilds the same template with new\n    # nouns, so the actual paraphrase call here is identity (the variant is\n    # generated upstream in `_build_logic_cluster`).\n    return premises + \" \" + conclusion\n\n\ndef _negation_logic(conclusion: str) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Negation variant: the oracle answer flips.\n\n    Returns (question, opposite_label).\n    \"\"\"\n    tail = conclusion.strip()\n    if tail.lower().startswith(\"therefore,\"):\n        tail = tail[len(\"therefore,\"):].strip()\n    # Question is \"Is it NOT the case that <conclusion>?\" \u2014 yes iff conclusion is false.\n    # The model's answer to \"Is the conclusion invalid?\" flips the original label.\n    tail_clean = tail.rstrip(\"?. \")\n    question = f\"Is it NOT the case that {tail_clean}?\"\n    return question, \"FLIPPED\"  # marker; the scoring layer flips the response\n\n\ndef _inverse_arithmetic(seed_question: str, seed_answer: int, a: int) -> tuple[str, int]:\n    \"\"\"Inverse variant for arithmetic: 'additive identity' \u2014 ask for the first\n    addend (a). The oracle answer differs from the seed, so this is the\n    'inverse/control' role rather than 'contrapositive equivalent'.\n    \"\"\"\n    return (\n        f\"(Inverse) Consider a problem with the same setup as: '{seed_question}'. \"\n        f\"What was the original starting quantity (the first number mentioned)?\",\n        a,\n    )\n\n\ndef _negation_arithmetic(seed_question: str, seed_answer: int) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Negation variant for arithmetic: a yes/no question with a *fixed*\n    deterministic oracle (independent of the model's seed answer).\n\n    We ask \"Is the answer to this problem equal to <wrong_value>?\" \u2014 the\n    oracle is \"NO\" (since the wrong value is, by construction, not the\n    seed answer). The coherence layer treats this as a binary claim the\n    model can answer YES/NO. We do NOT fold it into the same response\n    space as the seed; instead, the relational invariant is that the\n    negation's oracle is fixed and the model must agree with it.\n    \"\"\"\n    wrong = seed_answer + 1\n    question = (\n        f\"Consider: {seed_question} Is the answer to this problem equal to {wrong}? \"\n        f\"Answer YES or NO only.\"\n    )\n    return question, \"NO\"\n\n\ndef _paraphrase_arithmetic(seed_question: str, seed_answer: int, name1: str,\n                           name2: str, item: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Noun-swap paraphrase. The seed question will be rebuilt upstream with\n    fresh nouns; here we just return the seed form.\"\"\"\n    return seed_question\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Cluster builders\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n@dataclass\nclass Variant:\n    role: str            # 'seed' | 'paraphrase' | 'negation' | 'contrapositive' | 'inverse'\n    question: str\n    oracle: str | int    # canonical answer; for negation it is 'FLIPPED'\n    raw_question: str = \"\"  # original phrasing for logging\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass MIC:\n    cluster_id: str\n    domain: str           # 'logic' | 'arithmetic'\n    template_id: str\n    variants: dict[str, Variant] = field(default_factory=dict)\n    answers: dict[str, str | int] = field(default_factory=dict)\n    relations: dict[str, bool] = field(default_factory=dict)\n    difficulty_hint: str = \"medium\"\n    oracle_correct: str | int = \"\"\n\n\ndef _build_logic_cluster(idx: int, rng: random.Random) -> MIC:\n    \"\"\"Build one logic MIC using a randomly-chosen template + nouns.\"\"\"\n    template_id, builder = rng.choice(LOGIC_TEMPLATES)\n    A = rng.choice(LOGIC_NOUNS)\n    B = rng.choice([n for n in LOGIC_NOUNS if n != A])\n    C = rng.choice([n for n in LOGIC_NOUNS if n not in (A, B)])\n    premises, conclusion, label = builder(A, B, C)\n    seed_question = premises + \" \" + conclusion\n\n    # Paraphrase: same template, fresh nouns from the paraphrase pool\n    A2 = rng.choice(LOGIC_NOUNS_PARAPHRASE)\n    B2 = rng.choice([n for n in LOGIC_NOUNS_PARAPHRASE if n != A2])\n    C2 = rng.choice([n for n in LOGIC_NOUNS_PARAPHRASE if n not in (A2, B2)])\n    _, _, _ = builder(A2, B2, C2)\n    p2_premises, p2_conclusion, _ = builder(A2, B2, C2)\n    paraphrase_question = p2_premises + \" \" + p2_conclusion\n\n    # Negation: question + flipped\n    neg_question, neg_label = _negation_logic(conclusion)\n\n    # Contrapositive: rephrasing that holds iff original does\n    contra_question = _contrapositive(premises, conclusion)\n\n    cluster_id = f\"logic_{idx:04d}\"\n\n    mic = MIC(\n        cluster_id=cluster_id,\n        domain=\"logic\",\n        template_id=template_id,\n        difficulty_hint=_difficulty_hint_logic(template_id),\n        oracle_correct=label,\n    )\n    mic.variants = {\n        \"seed\": Variant(role=\"seed\", question=seed_question, oracle=label, raw_question=seed_question),\n        \"paraphrase\": Variant(role=\"paraphrase\", question=paraphrase_question, oracle=label, raw_question=paraphrase_question),\n        \"negation\": Variant(role=\"negation\", question=neg_question, oracle=neg_label, raw_question=neg_question),\n        \"contrapositive\": Variant(role=\"contrapositive\", question=contra_question, oracle=label, raw_question=contra_question),\n    }\n    mic.answers = {\n        \"seed\": label,\n        \"paraphrase\": label,\n        \"negation\": \"FLIPPED\",\n        \"contrapositive\": label,\n    }\n    mic.relations = {\n        \"paraphrase_eq_seed\": True,\n        \"negation_eq_not_seed\": True,\n        \"contrapositive_eq_seed\": True,\n    }\n    return mic\n\n\ndef _difficulty_hint_logic(template_id: str) -> str:\n    if template_id in (\"T1\", \"T4\", \"T5\", \"T10\"):\n        return \"easy\"\n    if template_id in (\"T2\", \"T7\", \"T11\", \"T12\"):\n        return \"medium\"\n    return \"hard\"\n\n\ndef _build_arithmetic_cluster(idx: int, rng: random.Random) -> MIC:\n    \"\"\"Build one arithmetic MIC.\"\"\"\n    template_id, builder = rng.choice(ARITHMETIC_TEMPLATES)\n\n    # Generate template-appropriate operands (all in [2,25], integer results).\n    # Per-template constraints: AS2 needs a > b; AS7 needs a % b == 0;\n    # AS11 picks big/small internally; AS12 needs a*b <= 100 (no absurd counts).\n    for _ in range(80):\n        a = rng.randint(2, 25)\n        b = rng.randint(2, 25)\n        c = rng.randint(2, 25)\n        # Per-template constraints\n        if template_id == \"AS2\" and a <= b:\n            continue\n        if template_id == \"AS7\" and (a % b != 0):\n            continue\n        if template_id == \"AS12\" and a * b > 100:\n            continue\n        name1 = rng.choice(NAMES_A)\n        name2 = rng.choice([n for n in NAMES_B if n != name1])\n        item = rng.choice(ITEMS)\n        out = builder(name1, name2, item, a, b, c)\n        ans = out[\"answer\"]\n        # require positive integer result\n        if isinstance(ans, int) and ans > 0:\n            break\n    else:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"arithmetic generator failed to produce positive answer\")\n\n    seed_question = out[\"question\"]\n    seed_answer = out[\"answer\"]\n\n    # Paraphrase: rebuild with fresh names + items\n    name1b = rng.choice(NAMES_B)\n    name2b = rng.choice([n for n in NAMES_A if n != name1b])\n    itemb = rng.choice(ITEMS_PARAPHRASE)\n    out2 = builder(name1b, name2b, itemb, a, b, c)\n    paraphrase_question = out2[\"question\"]\n\n    # Negation: a yes/no question whose oracle is \"NO\" (the wrong value is\n    # by construction not the seed answer).\n    neg_question, neg_label = _negation_arithmetic(seed_question, seed_answer)\n\n    # Inverse: ask for the original first addend\n    inv_question, inv_answer = _inverse_arithmetic(seed_question, seed_answer, a)\n\n    cluster_id = f\"arith_{idx:04d}\"\n    mic = MIC(\n        cluster_id=cluster_id,\n        domain=\"arithmetic\",\n        template_id=template_id,\n        difficulty_hint=_difficulty_hint_arith(seed_answer),\n        oracle_correct=seed_answer,\n    )\n    mic.variants = {\n        \"seed\": Variant(role=\"seed\", question=seed_question, oracle=seed_answer, raw_question=seed_question),\n        \"paraphrase\": Variant(role=\"paraphrase\", question=paraphrase_question, oracle=seed_answer, raw_question=paraphrase_question),\n        \"negation\": Variant(role=\"negation\", question=neg_question, oracle=neg_label, raw_question=neg_question),\n        \"inverse\": Variant(role=\"inverse\", question=inv_question, oracle=inv_answer, raw_question=inv_question),\n    }\n    mic.answers = {\n        \"seed\": seed_answer,\n        \"paraphrase\": seed_answer,\n        \"negation\": \"NO\",\n        \"inverse\": inv_answer,\n    }\n    mic.relations = {\n        \"paraphrase_eq_seed\": True,\n        \"negation_eq_no\": True,\n        \"inverse_distinct\": True,  # inverse has a different oracle answer\n    }\n    return mic\n\n\ndef _difficulty_hint_arith(ans: int) -> str:\n    if ans <= 10:\n        return \"easy\"\n    if ans <= 25:\n        return \"medium\"\n    return \"hard\"\n\n\n# =============================================================================\n# v2 NEW DOMAINS\n# =============================================================================\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Domain 3: Multi-hop Reading Comprehension (LGMT precedent)\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n# 30+ day names for the seed stories\nRC_DAYS = [\n    \"Monday\", \"Tuesday\", \"Wednesday\", \"Thursday\", \"Friday\",\n    \"Saturday\", \"Sunday\",\n]\n# 30+ place names\nRC_PLACES = [\n    \"Quito\", \"Reykjavik\", \"Lagos\", \"Hanoi\", \"Cairo\", \"Lima\", \"Oslo\",\n    \"Madrid\", \"Bogota\", \"Lisbon\", \"Athens\", \"Vienna\", \"Helsinki\",\n    \"Stockholm\", \"Warsaw\", \"Seoul\", \"Manila\", \"Nairobi\", \"Addis Ababa\",\n    \"Riga\", \"Bratislava\", \"Tunis\", \"Casablanca\", \"Kyiv\", \"Sofia\",\n    \"Tbilisi\", \"Yerevan\", \"Tashkent\", \"Colombo\", \"Kathmandu\",\n]\n# 30+ verb phrases\nRC_VERBS = [\n    \"walked\", \"bought\", \"donated\", \"found\", \"read\", \"painted\",\n    \"cooked\", \"mended\", \"shipped\", \"sketched\", \"fixed\", \"carved\",\n    \"lost\", \"sewed\", \"photographed\", \"packed\", \"taught\", \"sold\",\n    \"polished\", \"planted\", \"watered\", \"measured\", \"wrote\",\n    \"drew\", \"carried\", \"lifted\", \"sorted\", \"labeled\", \"stacked\",\n    \"loaded\",\n]\n# 30+ nouns\nRC_NOUNS = [\n    \"ledger\", \"fence\", \"lantern\", \"ledger\", \"envelope\", \"bicycle\",\n    \"scroll\", \"vase\", \"pencil\", \"cushion\", \"shelf\", \"toolbox\",\n    \"trowel\", \"compass\", \"whistle\", \"goblet\", \"shovel\", \"spool\",\n    \"napkin\", \"blanket\", \"teapot\", \"pitcher\", \"saddle\", \"lantern\",\n    \"lantern\", \"ledger\", \"letter\", \"parcel\", \"umbrella\", \"sandbag\",\n    \"lantern\",\n]\n# 30+ entity (subject) names\nRC_NAMES = [\n    \"Marisol\", \"Tomas\", \"Karim\", \"Inez\", \"Diego\", \"Lila\", \"Owen\",\n    \"Priya\", \"Beatrice\", \"Rafael\", \"Carmen\", \"Esme\", \"Felix\",\n    \"Greta\", \"Hassan\", \"Keiko\", \"Marco\", \"Nadia\", \"Pedro\",\n    \"Quincy\", \"Selma\", \"Uma\", \"Vera\", \"Wesley\", \"Ximena\",\n    \"Yusuf\", \"Zara\", \"Quinn\", \"Rosa\", \"Sami\", \"Tariq\",\n]\n\n\ndef _build_reading_cluster(idx: int, rng: random.Random) -> MIC:\n    \"\"\"Multi-hop reading comprehension MIC.\n\n    Variant roles:\n      seed         : a directly-answerable question about the story\n      paraphrase   : same story, different surface nouns/entities\n      negation     : a yes/no question whose oracle flips the seed answer\n      distractor   : the story is altered so the seed answer becomes WRONG;\n                     the oracle is the opposite of the seed answer.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Sample 4 sentences with distinct content\n    subject = rng.choice(RC_NAMES)\n    s_dog = rng.choice(RC_NAMES + [\"a dog named Pepper\", \"her dog Pepper\",\n                                    \"a cat named Whiskers\", \"her cat Whiskers\"])\n    place = rng.choice(RC_PLACES)\n    day = rng.choice(RC_DAYS)\n    verb1, verb2 = rng.sample(RC_VERBS, 2)\n    noun1, noun2 = rng.sample(RC_NOUNS, 2)\n    # The canonical story (in canonical form for question grounding):\n    canon_sentences = [\n        f\"{subject} owns a small bookstore in {place}.\",\n        f\"Each morning {subject} walks {s_dog} along the river.\",\n        f\"Last {day} {subject} bought a new {noun1} from the stationer.\",\n        f\"On Friday {subject} donated three boxes of children's books to the school library.\",\n    ]\n    seed_story = \" \".join(canon_sentences)\n    # Choose the seed question template (we keep things simple):\n    # The seed question asks about the noun on a specific day (M3 from the plan).\n    seed_q = f\"On what day did {subject} buy a {noun1}?\"\n    seed_a = day\n\n    # Paraphrase: re-tell the story with new content but the same day\n    sub2 = rng.choice([n for n in RC_NAMES if n != subject])\n    place2 = rng.choice([p for p in RC_PLACES if p != place])\n    day2 = day  # must match\n    noun1b = rng.choice([n for n in RC_NOUNS if n != noun1])\n    para_story = (\n        f\"{sub2} runs a small boutique in {place2}. \"\n        f\"Every evening {sub2} walks {s_dog} along the canal. \"\n        f\"Last {day2} {sub2} bought a new {noun1b} from the market. \"\n        f\"On Friday {sub2} donated a crate of old magazines to the local school.\"\n    )\n    para_q = f\"On what day did {sub2} buy a {noun1b}?\"\n    para_a = day2  # identical oracle\n\n    # Negation: yes/no question that flips the seed answer\n    # \"Did {subject} buy a {noun1} on {day}?\" -> YES\n    # Negation: \"Did {subject} NOT buy a {noun1} on {day}?\" -> NO\n    # The negation question asks whether the negation holds; the model\n    # says YES iff the negation is true. The flipped oracle is NO.\n    neg_q = f\"Is it NOT the case that {subject} bought a {noun1} on {day}?\"\n    neg_a = \"NO\"  # because subject DID buy it\n\n    # Distractor: change the day -> seed question now points to wrong answer\n    wrong_day = rng.choice([d for d in RC_DAYS if d != day])\n    distractor_story = seed_story.replace(day, wrong_day)\n    dist_q = f\"On what day did {subject} buy a {noun1}?\"\n    # The correct answer is now `wrong_day` (re-derived from the altered story)\n    dist_a = wrong_day\n\n    cluster_id = f\"read_{idx:04d}\"\n    mic = MIC(\n        cluster_id=cluster_id,\n        domain=\"reading\",\n        template_id=\"RC1\",\n        difficulty_hint=\"medium\",\n        oracle_correct=seed_a,\n    )\n    mic.variants = {\n        \"seed\": Variant(role=\"seed\", question=seed_q, oracle=seed_a,\n                         raw_question=seed_story + \" | \" + seed_q),\n        \"paraphrase\": Variant(role=\"paraphrase\", question=para_q, oracle=para_a,\n                              raw_question=para_story + \" | \" + para_q),\n        \"negation\": Variant(role=\"negation\", question=neg_q, oracle=neg_a,\n                            raw_question=seed_story + \" | \" + neg_q),\n        \"distractor\": Variant(role=\"distractor\", question=dist_q, oracle=dist_a,\n                              raw_question=distractor_story + \" | \" + dist_q),\n    }\n    mic.answers = {\n        \"seed\": seed_a,\n        \"paraphrase\": para_a,\n        \"negation\": neg_a,\n        \"distractor\": dist_a,\n    }\n    mic.relations = {\n        \"paraphrase_eq_seed\": True,\n        \"negation_eq_no\": True,\n        \"distractor_distinct_from_seed\": True,\n    }\n    return mic\n\n\n# Whiskers\"])\n    place = rng.choice(RC_PLACES)\n    day = rng.choice(RC_DAYS)\n    verb1, verb2 = rng.sample(RC_VERBS, 2)\n    noun1, noun2 = rng.sample(RC_NOUNS, 2)\n    # The canonical story (in canonical form for question grounding):\n    canon_sentences = [\n        f\"{subject} owns a small bookstore in {place}.\",\n        f\"Each morning {subject} walks {s_dog} along the river.\",\n        f\"Last {day} {subject} bought a new {noun1} from the stationer.\",\n        f\"On Friday {subject} donated three boxes of children's books to the school library.\",\n    ]\n    seed_story = \" \".join(canon_sentences)\n    # Choose the seed question template (we keep things simple):\n    # The seed question asks about the noun on a specific day (M3 from the plan).\n    seed_q = f\"On what day did {subject} buy a {noun1}?\"\n    seed_a = day\n\n    # Paraphrase: re-tell the story with new content but the same day\n    sub2 = rng.choice([n for n in RC_NAMES if n != subject])\n    place2 = rng.choice([p for p in RC_PLACES if p != place])\n    day2 = day  # must match\n    noun1b = rng.choice([n for n in RC_NOUNS if n != noun1])\n    para_story = (\n        f\"{sub2} runs a small boutique in {place2}. \"\n        f\"Every evening {sub2} walks {s_dog} along the canal. \"\n        f\"Last {day2} {sub2} bought a new {noun1b} from the market. \"\n        f\"On Friday {sub2} donated a crate of old magazines to the local school.\"\n    )\n    para_q = f\"On what day did {sub2} buy a {noun1b}?\"\n    para_a = day2  # identical oracle\n\n    # Negation: yes/no question that flips the seed answer\n    # \"Did {subject} buy a {noun1} on {day}?\" -> YES\n    # Negation: \"Did {subject} NOT buy a {noun1} on {day}?\" -> NO\n    # The negation question asks whether the negation holds; the model\n    # says YES iff the negation is true. The flipped oracle is NO.\n    neg_q = f\"Is it NOT the case that {subject} bought a {noun1} on {day}?\"\n    neg_a = \"NO\"  # because subject DID buy it\n\n    # Distractor: change the day -> seed question now points to wrong answer\n    wrong_day = rng.choice([d for d in RC_DAYS if d != day])\n    distractor_story = seed_story.replace(day, wrong_day)\n    dist_q = f\"On what day did {subject} buy a {noun1}?\"\n    # The correct answer is now `wrong_day` (re-derived from the altered story)\n    dist_a = wrong_day\n\n    cluster_id = f\"read_{idx:04d}\"\n    mic = MIC(\n        cluster_id=cluster_id,\n        domain=\"reading\",\n        template_id=\"RC1\",\n        difficulty_hint=\"medium\",\n        oracle_correct=seed_a,\n    )\n    mic.variants = {\n        \"seed\": Variant(role=\"seed\", question=seed_q, oracle=seed_a,\n                         raw_question=seed_story + \" | \" + seed_q),\n        \"paraphrase\": Variant(role=\"paraphrase\", question=para_q, \"yara\",\n        \"neg_x_is_B\": False, \"x_is_A\": True, \"y_is_A\": True,\n        \"x_is_B\": True, \"y_is_B\": True,\n        \"x_is_C\": True, \"y_is_C\": True, \"z_is_C\": True,\n
